To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the XXZ model at finite Trotter direction is equivalent to a system of two coupled deformed Schrödinger equations, with a potential that is a deformation of the harmonic potential, with deformation parameter equal to the Trotter direction, and with the deformation being a function of the anisotropy parameter.
the Matsubara correlation functions of the fermionic basis of local operators are expressed as deformed Abelian (hyper)elliptic integrals of the first and second kind.

the Matsubara correlator ω(ξ, ζ) is the canonical differential of the deformed elliptic integrals, and the Matsubara ratio is given by ρ(ζ)=exp(-2πI(ζ)) where I(ζ) is the deformed complete elliptic integral.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the computation of the following integral: \[ \int_{\mathbb{T}^2} \omega(\zeta_1, \zeta_2) \omega(\zta_1, \xi) \rho(\xi) d\xi, \] where ρ is the density of states of the XXZ model and ω is the correlator of the fermionic operators, and we show how it is reduced to the computation of the integral of ρ over the unit
the computation of the canonical differential of the deformed Abelian integral, and with the construction of the deformed period map.
the computation of the following quantity: ⟨ exp (ζ∑ j (a j + b j )) exp (ξ∑ j (c j + d j ))⟩, where a j, b j, c j and d j are fermionic operators acting on the Matsubara sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Matsubara correlation functions are expressed as deformed Abelian differentials of a Riemann surface.
we have found an explicit expression for the canonical differential in the theory deformed Abelian integral, which is a generalization of the Riemann theta function.
, in the XXZ spin chain, the Grassmann algebra of local operators is naturally extended to a Grassmann algebra of quasi-local operators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a theory of deformed integrals of motion for quantum spin chains, with a Grassmann algebra as a basic structure.
the XXZ chain is a deformation of the hypergeometric equation, in the sense that it is the equation for the canonical first kind deformed Abelian integral.
the hidden Grassmann structure in quantum spin systems is a deformation of the canonical theory of Abelian integrals, in the same way that quantum groups are deformations of the classical groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the infinite Trotter limit, the temperature correlation function is expressed as the sum of the two quantities, ρ(ζ)+ω(ζ,ξ).
ρ(ζ), which is the key object of the theory, is a function of the spectral parameter ζ only.
the computation of ρ(ζ), ω(ζ,ξ) is equivalent to the solution of a Riemann–Hilbert problem.
